objections.claim: The spec asserts that feeding a missing/empty/non-string `producer_id` through `verifyAuthLeg`/`evaluateDecisionRequest` yields the *existing* `producer-auth-failed` outcome, byte-identical to pre-conversion. The code shows this is false for `verifyAuthLeg`: today a malformed `producer_id` never reaches a brand check — `deriveKey` stringifies any value (`Buffer.from(String(producerId), "utf8")`) and the subsequent `verifyRecord` fails, so the recorded reason is `producer-auth-mismatch`, not `producer-auth-failed`. The conversion's `tryAsProducerId` → `null` → mapped to `producer-auth-failed` (per the spec's own mapping) changes that reason string. The spec's S8 test, as written, asserts the *post-conversion* outcome, so it cannot prove byte-identical behaviour — it would fail against the pre-conversion code it claims to preserve.
objections.evidence: `verifyAuthLeg` in `commissaire.js` pushes `{ reason: "producer-auth-mismatch" }` when `verifyRecord` fails, and `deriveKey` in `producer-auth.js` accepts any value via `String(producerId)`; the spec's §3 says "maps `null` to the existing deny/skip/`producer-auth-failed` outcome" and S8 asserts "byte-identical to pre-conversion behaviour".
objections.predicted_consequence: the S8 test either fails against the pre-conversion baseline (proving nothing) or passes against the new behaviour while the spec's "no observable behaviour change on a malformed record" guarantee is silently violated for `verifyAuthLeg` — the exact path the spec's own DONE item names.

objections.claim: The check flags *every* `as`/`<T>` assertion regardless of target type, allow-listing only "the validator mint sites (`asProducerId`, `asContractRevisionId`, `tryAs*`, any sibling `as<Brand>`)" plus the typed-`require` line. But `parseGovernedRecord`/`parseAdmissionRecord` — the validators the spec itself mandates — must access fields on `unknown`; the natural implementation is `raw as Record<string, unknown>`, which is an `AsExpression` targeting a non-brand type and is therefore flagged. The spec names no allow-list entry for these structural casts, and no cast-free implementation style is mandated. Separately, narrowing `readJson` to `unknown` forces validators for every shape it reads — the governor file (`{sk, pk, pk_fingerprint, master_secret}`, read in four places), the pk file, and `run-ledger.json` — but the spec names only `parseGovernedRecord` and `parseAdmissionRecord`. Either the build fails on legitimate validator casts, or the allow-list and validator inventory must expand beyond what the spec names, weakening the very guarantee the check exists to enforce.
objections.evidence: §3 "Boundary-contract check" says "Fail on any node whose enclosing function/declaration is not on the allow-list: the validator mint sites … and the single typed-require module-binding line"; §3 "Brands flow at every boundary" names only `parseGovernedRecord`/`parseAdmissionRecord`; `verifyAuthLeg`/`cmdRequestDecision`/`cmdTerminalVerdict` all call `readJson(governorFileOf(...))` on a shape no named validator covers.
objections.predicted_consequence: the `node --test` leg of `check-no-boundary-cast.mjs` exits non-zero on the real sources (the natural validator implementation trips property 1), forcing either contorted `Object.entries`-style validators the spec never specifies or an un-named allow-list expansion that re-opens the implicit-cast path the check was built to close.

objections.claim: The spec's validated-input-boundary list includes "on-disk JSON/JSONL … `events.jsonl`", but the read of `events.jsonl` happens inside `mintIssueAnchor` in `events.js` (governance, unconverted, stays `.js`). `commissaire.ts` calls `mintIssueAnchor` as an opaque `.js` function; the conversion cannot validate what `events.js` reads. The boundary inventory overstates the surface the slice actually controls, and the `unknown`-reader discipline cannot be applied to a read that lives in an unconverted module.
objections.evidence: §3 "Validated input boundaries" lists `events.jsonl`; `cmdAuditAnchor` dispatches into `mintIssueAnchor` from `events.js`, which is not in the conversion scope.
objections.predicted_consequence: a reviewer or the build agent treats `events.jsonl` as a converted boundary, but the actual validation gap sits in `events.js` and is invisible to this slice's checks — the boundary list is not a faithful map of what the conversion governs.

objections.claim: No named test can distinguish a `commissaire.ts` whose `producer-auth` import is typed (`const producerAuth: ProducerAuthApi = require(...)`) from one whose import is untyped (`const producerAuth = require(...)`, i.e. `any`). With an untyped require, `producerAuth.deriveKey(rawString, ...)` compiles cleanly, so the slice's load-bearing model — a raw string at a `deriveKey` call is a `tsc` error on the production path — is false while every named check passes.
objections.evidence: DONE item "types its `producer-auth` import via `import type` + typed `require` so brands flow across the edge"; §3 "The typed-`require` module binding is the sanctioned trusted-sibling binding". S2 tests a standalone fixture (`test/fixtures/ts-brand-negative/`), explicitly "not the real `commissaire.ts`", so it proves the brand types exist in isolation, not that the real edge is typed. S4a (`tsc --noEmit` on the real sources) passes with an `any`-typed require. The cast-prohibition check's property 1 collects only `AsExpression`/`TypeAssertionExpression` nodes; the typed-require line is a type annotation, not a cast, so it produces no node for the allow-list to admit — the allow-list entry is vacuous and the check cannot detect either the line's absence or its untyped form.
objections.predicted_consequence: A build that ships `const producerAuth = require("./producer-auth")` (no type annotation) satisfies S2, S3, S4a, S4b, S5 and every DONE item except the one unverifiable line; the central "brands flow across the real production edge" claim is silently false and the DONE item cannot be decided.

objections.claim: The existing outcome for a record with a missing/empty/non-string `producer_id` in `verifyAuthLeg` is a failure with reason `producer-auth-mismatch` (`deriveKey(master, undefined, …)` derives a key from `"undefined"`, the HMAC mismatches, a failure is pushed). It is not a skip, and `producer-auth-failed` is `evaluateDecisionRequest`'s reason, not `verifyAuthLeg`'s. The S8/DONE test asserts "deny / `producer-auth-failed` / skip" — a disjunction that includes "skip", which is not the pre-conversion outcome. A conversion that maps `tryAsProducerId` → null → skip (dropping the record from the failures array) makes `verifyAuthLeg.pass` true for a malformed record that today fails closed, and the test as written accepts it.
objections.evidence: S8 scenario ("the outcome is the existing deny / `producer-auth-failed` / skip (byte-identical to pre-conversion behaviour)"); DONE item "mapping `null` to the existing deny/skip/`producer-auth-failed` outcome, preserving the current fail-closed-on-malformed behaviour". The current `verifyAuthLeg` code path (`producer-auth-mismatch`) is in the diff under review.
objections.predicted_consequence: A build that turns a today-failing malformed record into a tolerated skip passes S8 (membership in the disjunction) while violating the DONE item's own "preserving the current fail-closed-on-malformed behaviour" — the security-relevant outcome (a malformed record silently passing the auth leg) changes undetected. "Byte-identical" and a three-way disjunction cannot both be the oracle; the spec must pin the exact per-function outcome (e.g. `producer-auth-mismatch` for `verifyAuthLeg`).

objections.claim: `producer-auth.ts` (like the current `producer-auth.js`) only exports `producerAuthSelftest`; it does not invoke it at load. "`producer-auth.ts` runs directly under Node 22.18+ type-stripping (its `producerAuthSelftest()` exits 0)" names no command — `node bin/lib/producer-auth.ts` would exit 0 without running the selftest, and the alternative (`node -e "require('./bin/lib/producer-auth.ts').producerAuthSelftest()"`) depends on `require()` of a `.ts` file being supported on the exact Node minor, which the spec itself lists as an unvalidated assumption ("confirm the exact minor against Node release notes").
objections.evidence: S4c scenario; §7 Assumptions ("the dev/source lane runs on Node ≥ 22.18 … Validate: confirm the exact minor").
objections.predicted_consequence: The S4c DONE item cannot be run as written — a test author must invent the invocation, and if `require()` of `.ts` is unsupported on the validated minor the scenario fails for a reason the spec did not pin.

objections.claim: Several DONE items are decidable only by inspection or by an unstated procedure: the CI wiring of `faff regions check` into `.github/workflows/validate.yml`; the README/AGENTS doc changes; the startup-timing recording ("recorded on this ticket"); the revert demonstration ("shown in the PR description"); and "byte-stable across two consecutive builds". None has a scenario, and the spec does not say what would be run/observed for them.
objections.evidence: DONE items "runs in CI (wired into the existing `.github/workflows/validate.yml` governance leg)", "startup recorded on this ticket", "Reverting the conversion commit restores the prior artifact … demonstrated in the PR description", "byte-stable across two consecutive builds".
objections.predicted_consequence: A reviewer cannot decide these items from the spec alone; each depends on an unstated artifact (workflow diff, ticket entry, PR prose) that a build could omit while every scenario passes.

objections.claim: The cast-prohibition check walks the real `producer-auth.ts` and `commissaire.ts` ASTs. To "plant" a `value as ProducerId`, `<ProducerId>value`, and an `as any` cast "at input boundaries outside a validator", the test must either copy the real sources with an injected cast or the check must accept a file-list parameter — neither mechanism is named, and the check's allow-list is keyed to the real sources' validator sites.
objections.evidence: S3 scenario; DONE item "a negative test plants a `value as ProducerId`, a `<ProducerId>value`, and an `as any` laundering cast at boundaries and proves the check exits non-zero on each".
objections.predicted_consequence: The negative test cannot be written from the spec; if the check hard-codes the real source paths, the planted fixture is never scanned and the test is vacuous.
